Satan, described at the verse’s end as forsaking the human being and failing to help.
For the human being; the one whom Satan leaves unsupported.

corrections: Installed all 293 supplied logical blocks in reviewed Persian and complete English. Each article includes eight sections, twenty-five subheadings, eight morphology cards, and eight Arabic quotation blocks: three full Quran verses, three lexical quotations, and two poetic witnesses. All quotation blocks have English transliteration. Exact supplied Arabic preserved; blockquote formatting alone removed.

No reassignment required. The conditional FormI imperfect, passive participle, and intensive adjective remain distinct.

Corrected araqi in the Adi poetic witness: the word refers to wooden crosspieces fastened across the bucket mouth, not rope or straps. Updated the Persian poetic rendering and its explanation, preserving the Arabic quotation. Identified the witness as describing a horse, as the primary lexical source reports.

Corrected the relationship of17:20to17:22: two verses earlier, rather than the immediately preceding verse. Clarified Raghib definition as withholding help by the person expected to assist. Completed shorthand verse references and marked all three full article verse translations as proposed, preserving installed translations.

Preserved the distinction between material separation, bodily weakness, and morally blameworthy withdrawal of help. Withholding divine help, being forsaken, and Satan’s abandonment are not equated ethically. Kept the distinction between blameworthy and unsupported, and between leading astray and forsaking. Recorded both readings of the final25:29sentence speaker, with Tabari preference and Zamakhshari alternatives sourced.
